> **What this case shows** — SDNN, the standard deviation of the RR intervals, is the classical HRV
> spread, but it is inflated by the ectopic beats and big respiratory swings that make the RR distribution
> non-Gaussian. The **interquartile range** is the robust alternative. This case adds one
> (**`interquartileRange`**). On real Fantasia RR intervals it reproduces **two** references —
> **`scipy.stats.iqr`** *and* base R **`IQR`** — **bit-for-bit**. And it tells us something SDNN hides:
> the RR distribution is heavy-tailed, so the robust spread (56.3 ms) sits well below SDNN (73.7 ms).

::: {.callout-tip title="The recipe you'll learn"}
**Workflow** — `interquartileRange(x)` → the robust spread of the middle 50%.
**Way of thinking** — compare a robust spread with SDNN. When they agree, the RR distribution is roughly
Gaussian; when the robust spread runs *below* SDNN, a heavy tail (ectopy, large RSA) is inflating SDNN.
The ratio is a free non-normality flag.
**Ecosystem usage** — `PhysioAnalysis::interquartileRange()`, alongside `medianAbsDev()` and `signalMoments()`.
:::

## Proposition

On real Fantasia RR intervals, the new `interquartileRange` reproduces both `scipy.stats.iqr` and base R
`IQR` bit-for-bit (IQR = 76 ms, `|diff|` = 0 against each); and because the RR distribution is
heavy-tailed (excess kurtosis 7.17, skewness 0.07), the robust IQR-based SD estimate (56.3 ms) sits below
SDNN (73.7 ms; ratio 0.76) — the opposite of the near-Gaussian EEG, where the robust scale matched the SD.

## Question & goal

**The question is a gap and a shape: the ecosystem had SDNN and a deviation-based robust scale but no
quantile-based robust spread — can a new op reproduce the two references exactly, and what does the
robust-vs-classical comparison say about the RR distribution?** The goal is to introduce
`interquartileRange`, certify it against both, and use the ratio as a shape diagnostic.

## Challenge & approach

The IQR is `Q3 − Q1`, with quartiles from R's default type-7 quantile (the same linear interpolation as
`scipy.stats.iqr` and `numpy.percentile`) — an order statistic, so it matches any correct implementation
exactly. We check it against both references on the identical RR vector, and compare the normal-consistent
IQR scale `IQR/(2·Φ⁻¹(0.75))` with SDNN.

```
Fantasia RR (392 intervals) → interquartileRange (Q3-Q1, type 7) → IQR = 76 ms
                             vs scipy.stats.iqr → |diff| = 0   ·   vs base R IQR → |diff| = 0
                             robust IQR-scale = 56.3 ms   <   SDNN = 73.7 ms   (ratio 0.76)
                             RR is heavy-tailed (exkurt 7.17, skew 0.07) → SDNN inflated by the tails
```

## Data

**Fantasia (PhysioNet)**: subject **f1y01** (young healthy adult), first **5-minute RR window** (392
intervals) — the same RR the [poincare-hrv](../poincare-hrv-fantasia/index.qmd) and
[hrv-dfa](../hrv-dfa-aging-fantasia/index.qmd) cases use. Details in
[`artifacts/data_sources.json`](artifacts/data_sources.json).

## Results

![Left: the RR-interval histogram — near-symmetric but heavy-tailed (isolated short and long intervals at both extremes), with the IQR band (724–800 ms) shaded, the median (blue), and the mean ± SDNN band (red). Right: the robust-scale/SDNN ratio as a distribution-shape diagnostic — for this heavy-tailed RR it is 0.76 (SDNN inflated by the tails), versus 1.002 for the near-Gaussian eyes-closed EEG of the median-abs-dev case.](artifacts/figure.png)

*How to read this:* left — a compact core with isolated outliers at both extremes is the mark of heavy tails; the
IQR spans only the dense middle. Right — a ratio at 1 means Gaussian (EEG); a ratio below 1 means a heavy
tail is inflating SDNN (RR).

| Quantity | Value |
|---|--:|
| **IQR** (`interquartileRange`) | **76 ms** |
| quartiles Q1 / Q3 | 724 / 800 ms |
| vs `scipy.stats.iqr` / base R `IQR` (\|diff\|) | **0** (bit-for-bit) |
| SDNN (classical) | 73.7 ms |
| robust IQR-scale / SDNN | **0.76** |
| RR skewness / excess kurtosis | 0.07 / **7.17** |

The new op equals both references exactly, and the ratio flags the tails. Values trace to
[`artifacts/iqr_summary.csv`](artifacts/iqr_summary.csv).

## Conclusion

`interquartileRange` completes the robust-dispersion toolkit (`signalMoments`, `medianAbsDev`), and it is
exact against two references. The transferable takeaway: **pair a robust spread with SDNN. On this RR
series they disagree — the robust IQR-scale is 24% below SDNN — because the RR distribution is heavy-tailed and
SDNN is pulled up by outliers in both tails. That divergence is the opposite of the near-Gaussian EEG, where the robust
scale and the SD agreed; the ratio itself tells you the distribution's shape.**

## Open questions

- The robust/classical ratio drops below 1 exactly when the RR distribution departs from Gaussian, so it
  is a cheap non-normality / artifact flag for HRV: a ratio well below 1 says SDNN is being driven by a
  heavy tail (ectopy, large respiratory excursions), not uniform beat-to-beat variability. Pairing IQR
  with SDNN, or robust-cleaning the RR series first, separates the two. *Documented, not escalated.*

## Using this in your own analysis

| Step | Function | Package |
|---|---|---|
| Interquartile range (robust spread) | `interquartileRange()` | PhysioAnalysis |
| Deviation-based robust scale | `medianAbsDev()` | PhysioAnalysis |
| Classical SD / SDNN, skewness | `signalMoments()` | PhysioAnalysis |

**Reading the result.**

- **IQR** — a robust HRV spread in ms; a handful of ectopic beats barely moves it (unlike SDNN).
- **robust-scale vs SDNN** — agreement ⇒ near-Gaussian RR; robust ≪ SDNN ⇒ a heavy tail is inflating SDNN.

**The recipe, copy-runnable:**

```r
library(PhysioAnalysis)

interquartileRange(rr)                      # robust HRV spread (ms)
interquartileRange(rr) / (2 * qnorm(0.75))  # robust SD estimate; compare to sd(rr) = SDNN
# reproduces scipy.stats.iqr and base R IQR bit-for-bit.
```

**Auditing the numbers.** Every value on this page traces to
[`artifacts/iqr_summary.csv`](artifacts/iqr_summary.csv), and [`audit.py`](audit.py) re-checks the IQR,
the quartiles, the bit-exact match against scipy and base R, the robust-vs-SDNN ratio, and the honestly
noted scope (new quantile-based robust op; double-reference machine precision; the distribution-shape
diagnostic; the contrast with the near-Gaussian median-abs-dev case).

## Erratum (PhysioRecipes 0.7.2) {#erratum}

The distribution-shape finding on this page was **re-authored** in release
0.7.2, not merely renumbered. Earlier releases reported the RR distribution as
*right-skewed* (skewness 1.01) — that skew was an artefact of a reader defect.

`PhysioIO::readWFDB()` mis-defaulted the signal baseline on headers that state
the gain without a `(baseline)` annex, which is the Fantasia header style,
offsetting the ECG by exactly one physical unit. Under the offset the R-peak
detector missed a beat in this five-minute window, and the resulting
double-length interval produced an apparent right tail. Fixed in PhysioIO
0.2.7; the corrected reader agrees with the reference implementation
`wfdb-python` **bit-for-bit** (max |difference| = 0) on this record, and the RR
series was re-extracted (391 → 392 intervals).

With the corrected data the distribution is **near-symmetric but heavy-tailed**
(skewness 0.07, excess kurtosis 7.17): outlying intervals sit in *both* tails.
The case's core result is unchanged and, if anything, sharper — the robust
IQR-scale still sits far below SDNN (ratio 0.76), and `interquartileRange`
still reproduces `scipy.stats.iqr` and base R `IQR` bit-for-bit.

The correction also demonstrates the case's own thesis on real data: it moved
SDNN by 4.4 ms (69.3 → 73.7) while leaving the **IQR at exactly 76 ms**. The
classical statistic absorbed the change; the robust one did not notice it.

The case's audit invariant was updated accordingly — from "skewness > 0.5" to
"excess kurtosis > 3 and |skewness| < 0.5" — so that the automated check
enforces the finding actually being claimed.
